content:
Hi! I would like to ask for guidance about the boundary between mathlib and CSLib for relation-level rewriting API.

I opened a small PR adding names/API around confluence-style properties for relations, motivated by the existing theorem Relation.church_rosser in mathlib:

https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/pull/40368

The PR currently adds predicates such as Relation.Confluent, Relation.ChurchRosser, and Relation.StronglyConfluent, together with basic API like Confluent ↔ ChurchRosser.

The downstream motivation is a polynomial reduction development for MvPolynomial / Gröbner bases. In that development, one-step polynomial reduction is defined as an ordinary relation on MvPolynomial, and then the usual relation closures are used directly. For example, the intended setup has the following shape:

def MonomialOrder.ReducesToSet
    (m : MonomialOrder σ)
    (P : Set (MvPolynomial σ R))
    (f g : MvPolynomial σ R) : Prop :=
  ∃ p ∈ P, m.ReducesToPoly p f g

scoped[Reduction] notation:50 f:51 " ⟶*[" m ", " P "] " g:51 =>
  Relation.ReflTransGen (MonomialOrder.ReducesToSet m P) f g

scoped[Reduction] notation:50 f:51 " ⟷*[" m ", " P "] " g:51 =>
  Relation.EqvGen (MonomialOrder.ReducesToSet m P) f g

scoped[Reduction] notation:50 f:51 " ↓[" m ", " P "] " g:51 =>
  Relation.Join
    (Relation.ReflTransGen (MonomialOrder.ReducesToSet m P)) f g

Then polynomial-specific results can be stated using relation-level notions such as well-foundedness and local confluence, for example:

theorem MonomialOrder.ReducesToSet.wellFounded
    (P : Set (MvPolynomial σ R)) :
    WellFounded (flip (m.ReducesToSet P))

theorem MonomialOrder.ReducesToSet.locallyConfluent_singleton
    {p : MvPolynomial σ R}
    (hpLC : IsUnit (m.leadingCoeff p)) :
    Relation.LocallyConfluent
      (m.ReducesToSet ({p} : Set (MvPolynomial σ R)))

I have also been experimenting with a WIP development continuing from this polynomial-reduction layer toward Buchberger's criterion. It seems to me that a polynomial reduction relation could provide a common specification layer for finite reduction, equivalence closure, joinability, normal forms, and the correctness of division-style algorithms or later algorithmic variants.

However, I was pointed to CSLib, which already contains more general relation-level rewriting API, including confluence, normal forms, normalizing relations, strong normalization, strong commutation, and Newman-style results. Looking again at the downstream development, it also seems possible that many of the general equivalence theorems between confluence, Church-Rosser, unique normal forms, etc. are not actually necessary for the first polynomial reduction / Buchberger criterion PRs. Some of those statements could be postponed, kept polynomial-specific, or avoided entirely.

So the main question I would like to ask is: when deciding what should live in mathlib versus CSLib, is it reasonable to use polynomial reduction / Gröbner bases as a mathlib use case for upstreaming only a minimal subset of the relation-level API?

Concretely, should mathlib have a small relation vocabulary around the existing Relation.church_rosser theorem, such as Confluent / ChurchRosser and perhaps only the pieces directly useful for polynomial reduction? Or should the general rewriting API remain in CSLib, with the polynomial reduction development in mathlib using only the existing Relation.ReflTransGen, Relation.EqvGen, and Relation.Join, plus polynomial-specific notions such as polynomial normal forms where needed?

I would be happy to adjust the PR accordingly. In particular, I can remove or postpone StronglyConfluent if that is too close to CSLib's more general strong commutation API, and keep the PR focused on whatever minimal relation-level vocabulary is considered appropriate for later MvPolynomial / Gröbner basis formalization.

To repeat myself from the PR, I'm happy as the primary author of this material in CSLib to upstream anything that is helpful for Mathlib. I was just surprised to see this since I'd previously had the impression this would be out of scope.

Just a brief follow-up to this discussion: I have opened a new draft PR containing the fuller polynomial-reduction development that motivated the earlier API question:

https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/pull/41475

Compared with #40368, this PR includes the actual downstream use case, including termination and normal forms for polynomial reduction, translation lemmas, and the reduction-theoretic Gröbner basis criterion. I have kept the general relation-level API limited to the parts used by this development.

If anyone is interested, I would greatly appreciate feedback on the PR, especially on whether the proposed boundary between mathlib and CSLib seems appropriate.
